references.text: The fulfillment of the instruction to gather double on the sixth day, where the people actually gathered double manna before the Sabbath.
The Sabbath command explaining why the sixth day required preparation—the seventh day was to be a day of rest.
Further instructions about the Sabbath and preparation, confirming the principle of finishing work before the day of rest.
The Sabbath regulation in the overview of the Lord's feasts, emphasizing the weekly rhythm of six days of work and one day of rest.
Jesus' prayer for daily bread in the Lord's Prayer, reflecting God's daily provision of manna to the people of Israel.
Jesus refers to the manna in the wilderness and presents himself as the true bread from heaven, in contrast to the manna that the fathers ate.
Complementary verses in the same account: 16:5 gives the instruction for double gathering, while 16:26 confirms the absence of manna on the Sabbath as the basis for the rule.
Direct narrative connection: 16:5 is the instruction for double gathering, while 16:22 documents that the people followed the order.
Theological context: 16:5 gives the command, while 16:29 explains the theological reasoning (God's gift of the Sabbath) and its consequence.
